PICK POCKET SQUAD

By: Nicky Troll | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A slick pick pocket squad is shamelessly targeting the elderly - they ‘re not hunting for wallets, they’re hunting for car keys!

Unique Selling Point:
A NEW CRIME TREND
CCTV FOOTAGE
ENDEARING OLD CHARACTERS


Further information:
A highly coordinated pickpocket squad is sweeping through shopping centres.

They hunt for car keys, not wallets by the time their victims realise what’s happened, the car’s gone. The brand doesn’t matter. But the targets stay the same. The elderly. The MO never changes – it’s super slick - lift the car keys, locate the vehicle, and vanish without a trace.

29 cases in 11 months. CCTV footage showing the MO. A stolen vehicle used as the getaway car in another pickpocket theft - an arrest on camera with the same car, yet the suspects were released.

As the victims pile up. The evidence stacks up but still, the pickpocket squad is out there, ready to pounce again.

STRUCTURE | PICK POCKET SQUAD

(MACFARLANE): They see you before you see them. Lurking. Waiting. Every move calculated… because each second counts.

(CAR THIEF SUBTITLE): We’ll have someone watching them. We have 30 minutes to pull it off.

(MACFARLANE): This isn’t your average pickpocket scam. By the time you realise what’s missing… it’s already too late. They’re not hunting wallets… they’re hunting cars.

(MACFARLANE): They rely on deception and their methods are worryingly successful.

(ADRIAAN): We call them chancers. They, they don't go for a specific brand.

(MACFARLANE): Adriaan de Klerk is from a security company tracking this crime trend.

(ADRIAAN): These ones, they take what they get. Whether it's a city golf from voetsek or it's a brand new Mercedes Benz. If they get the key and they can get away with the car, they’re gone.

(MACFARLANE): Getting the key is the trick. This CCTV clip reveals it’s a well-oiled routine.
What looks like regular trolley traffic is actually a practiced crew of three cornering their target. The seemingly innocent pile-up is the set-up. First, a quick distraction: the decoy keeps the target in position, while his accomplice lifts the keys… It’s so fast, the target doesn’t even register.
She casually steps away, and the handover is seamless.
(LIEB): We get about between 3 and 4 cases per week that is being reported, especially in the Pretoria area.

(MACFARLANE): The Insurance Crime Bureau, or ICB, is connecting the dots one stolen car at a time. Louwrens Liebenberg heads the investigation.

(LIEB): They target the smaller, shopping centers, because it's making it easier for them to identify the vehicle in the parking area.

(MACFARLANE): In this clip, you can see the pickpocket crew searching for their prize…..

But none of this relies on chance: they have a signature move.

(LIEB): It's different from other vehicle crime crews, they don't know what they are going to steal, they target a certain portion of the population.

(MACFARLANE): Different shops, same trick, same targets… The Elderly.

Gerhard Botha never saw it coming.

A routine grocery run in February took an unexpected turn.

(GERHARD SUBTITLE): When I walked out with my things, I saw my car was gone. And I checked my pocket and I realised I don’t have the key. I thought, “Wow, I really am getting old, I must’ve left the key in the car.” But then I thought, “No, something’s wrong here.”

(MACFARLANE) : CCTV footage fills in the gaps. It’s the same tactic: a distraction, a lift, and a hand over.

After seeing the footage Gerhard now knows nothing happened by coincidence that day. This crew came prepared, right down to their disguises.

(GERHARD SUBTITLE): When I got to the yoghurt, there was a woman in the way. I said to her, “Excuse me.” And she moved away, another man came past, and he had a face mask on and the woman had a hat on you, you know.

(MACFARLANE): The key was lifted in under a minute, a move the ICB has seen before.

(LIEB): They will pass this onto the third individual, and this individual will then go outside and start looking for the vehicle
(MACFARLANE): And that’s exactly what happened in Gerhard’s case - the outside footage shows the man who took the keys getting into the car and driving off.

(GERHARD SUBTITLE): But I’ll tell you it’s a big emotional shock for a person. Us elderly people, we stay in security complexes that are safe. But when we drive out of here, then anything can happen

(MACFARLANE): Gerhard wasn’t the first target… and he won’t be the last for the pickpocket crews.

Cars are a valuable prize for these criminals: stripped for parts, used as getaway vehicles or illegally exported.

(MACFARLANE): Adriaan is this a syndicate?
(ADRIAAN): We know about four groups. We've arrested them, we've chased them. At the beginning it was more like, a “kans-vat” [opportunistic] type of crime. And then they saw it was an easy thing. The amount of cars they are taking goes into a syndicate level immediately.

(MACFARLANE): There’s been more than 30 reported cases mostly in Pretoria in just 11 months. And those are the ones we know about.

Elsa van der Watt was targeted in April.

The footage shows the same shameless set-up. This crew knew what they were shopping for and didn’t waste time.

(ELSA SUBTITLE): I can see now how they box you in.
(MACFARLANE SUBTITLE): Ok
(ELSA SUBTITLE): See they’re looking for something up there, and then they pull it down on purpose. I can see it clearly now.
(MACFARLANE SUBTITLE): You’re even helping them!
(ELSA SUBTITLE): That’s what I’m saying. From bad to worse.
(MACFARLANE SUBTITLE): Is that where the keys were nicked?
(ELSA SUBTITLE): Yes, there goes the key.
(ELSA SUBTITLE): So easy, right?
It’s so unreal. It can’t be. The car can’t just drive off by itself. But hey, this is South Africa. [laughs]
(MACFARLANE SUBTITLE): It’s not supposed to be like that.
(ELSA SUBTITLE): And in our neighbourhood, four people we know have had their cars taken. The neighbour up the road, three women from our centre - all exactly the same way.
(MACFARLANE SUBTITLE): You, they’re sneaky! It’s disgusting what they’re doing.

(LIEB): The way they do it, you can see that they are getting away with it for quite substantial time. And and they are well organized. If you look at the number of vehicles left to be recovered, compared to the number of vehicles that's lost, there must be an element of organized crime involved in this, especially in the market receiving these vehicles.

(MACFARLANE): To understand the stolen car trade, we approached someone who knows it from the inside. He’s a self-confessed car thief and, while not tied to the pickpocket crews, he knows their market.

(CAR THIEF SUBTITLE): You see, a car that comes with keys is like a complete car.
(MACFARLANE): It’s the best…
(CAR THIEF): It’s the best.
(CAR THIEF SUBTITLE): There are no scratches, no broken glass, the ignition hasn’t been damaged. When people see a car like that, they pay good money.

(MACFARLANE): The brand doesn’t matter - every car has a buyer.

(MACFARLANE SUBTITLE): Where are the different markets?
(CAR THIEF SUBTITLE): Yah, any Toyota and legends even Ford Ranger, Raptor – you can name them. Those are the ones that cross the border
(MACFARLANE SUBTITLE): And the other ones? What happens with them?
(CAR THIEF SUBTITLE): Those are the ones we take to the local scrapyard. And the small cars, those are the ones that keep us from going broke. You get R10 000 to R15 000. But for an SUV that goes to the border, that’s like is R200 000.

(MACFARLANE): Older SUVs often get repurposed with fake number plates.

That’s what happened to Gerhard’s Honda. It was being used as a getaway vehicle in more pick pocket thefts.

In April, a tip-off came in. The car was spotted in an informal settlement outside Pretoria.

De Klerk and his team swooped on the thieves.

(ADRIAAN): We identified the vehicle on certain identifiable marks on the on the vehicle. As soon as they were driving the car we did a take down on them..

UPSOUND FROM ARREST DASH CAM CLIP.

(ADRIAAN): They won't give you information. They won't give up their friends. They are all they take the punishment and tomorrow's another day.

(MACFARLANE): Despite being caught with a stolen vehicle, the suspects were released on bail.

(MACFARLANE): The biggest issue with cracking this crime trend is it’s near impossible to catch and implicate the whole crew in a single car theft, and even harder to get the charges to stick…

(LIEB): The guy that you arrest in the vehicle is in possession of a stolen vehicle.But connecting the other two suspects in the group, connecting them is more difficult.
(MACFARLANE): Why isn’t a Sting operation viable in this particular crime trend?
(LIEB): It's not like you can predict they will be at the shopping center today. They hop all over the place. So the chances of getting them to basically pickpocket you is, is between all of those shoppers. It's very difficult to do a sting operation in that.

(MACFARLANE): And, just like the thieves, these incidents tend to slip through the cracks too, dismissed as petty crime by the police. Often, not even the damning CCTV footage is secured.

(GERHARD SUBTITLE): As for the police, they didn’t really seem interested. I even told them we’ve got a video of the incident, if you want to try to identify the people. They said, “No, the investigating officer will contact you if they need it.” And that’s the last I heard - that was that.

(LIEB): We are limited in the scope of what we can do. We are mandated by the insurance industry to investigate organized crime impacting the insurance industry. We will then be dependent on our partners in law enforcement to assist us in taking this case to a prosecution level. And, and that is our limitations. We can do a lot of things on our own, but in the end. We need law enforcement. Come on board and then to prosecute this is something else.

(MACFARLANE): In the meantime, the money is too big an attraction for the pick pocket squads.

(CAR THIEF SUBTITLE): With small cars, you know, if you take it to a scrapyard R20 000 - you’ll get that from a scarpyard. So, once you have a small car, you know you’re going to get R20 000. Even if it's just over R10000, you’ll take it. Because you want to go home with something.

(MACFARLANE): And, says the insider, this crime is likely to become more sophisticated.

(CAR THIEF SUBTITLE): These are beginners. It’s their first time stealing cars. So, that’s why, they know where to take it for small money. They are still learning the ropes. Especially the ones that are targeting the old people.
(MACFARLAN SUBTITLE): They’re still building confidence.
(CAR THIEF SUBTITLE): They are still building confidence to reach the next level.


(LIEB): If you keep your handbag with in the trolley, with your key sticking out, your cell phone sticking out.If you go into a pub and you sit down with the pub and you put down your wallet and your car key next to you, it is an opportunity to take that key and to take your vehicle. You are going to become a target irrespective of your age

(MACFARLANE): Because in this deceptive criminal game, all it takes… is one distraction, one key, and in a heartbeat your car is gone.


PROMOS
PROMO 1
(MACFARLANE): A slick pick pocket squad is operating in plain sight.

(ELSA SUBTITLE): Ek kan nou sien dat hulle jou af kamp.

(MACFARLANE): They‘re not hunting for wallets, they’re after car keys

(ELSA SUBTITLE): dis so onwerklik, dit kan nie wees nie, die kar kan nie van self ry nie.
(MACFARLANE): Hitting the same unsuspecting targets - the Elderly. We investigate this shameless scam.


PROMO 2
(MACFARLANE): Pick pocketing - once a petty crime, now leveled up…

(ADRIAAN): These ones, they take what they get. Whether it's a city golf from 19-voetsek or it's a brand new Mercedes Benz.
(MACFARLANE): A streetwise crew is on the loose - and business is good.

(LIEB): They target, a certain portion of the population
(MACFARLANE): They hunt car keys and target the elderly. We unpack this cunning crime trend.



PROMO 3
(MACFARLANE): What starts as petty pickpocketing ends with a stolen car - a brazen criminal crew is feeding the stolen car market, snatching keys with precision and flipping cars for profit.

(CAR THIEF SUBTITLE): There’s no scratches, there’s no broken glass, the ignition hasn’t been damaged. You see a car that comes with keys is like a complete car

(MACFARLANE): In this clip, you can see the pickpocket crew searching for their prize….. But none of this relies on chance: they have a signature move. (LIEB): It's different from other vehicle crime crews, they don't know what they are going to steal, they target a certain portion of the population. (MACFARLANE): Different shops, same trick, same targets… The Elderly. Gerhard Botha never saw it coming. A routine grocery run in February took an unexpected turn. (GERHARD SUBTITLE): When I walked out with my things, I saw my car was gone. And I checked my pocket and I realised I don’t have the key. I thought, “Wow, I really am getting old, I must’ve left the key in the car.” But then I thought, “No, something’s wrong here.” (MACFARLANE) : CCTV footage fills in the gaps. It’s the same tactic: a distraction, a lift, and a hand over. After seeing the footage Gerhard now knows nothing happened by coincidence that day. This crew came prepared, right down to their disguises. (GERHARD SUBTITLE): When I got to the yoghurt, there was a woman in the way. I said to her, “Excuse me.” And she moved away, another man came past, and he had a face mask on and the woman had a hat on you, you know. (MACFARLANE): The key was lifted in under a minute, a move the ICB has seen before. (LIEB): They will pass this onto the third individual, and this individual will then go outside and start looking for the vehicle (MACFARLANE): And that’s exactly what happened in Gerhard’s case - the outside footage shows the man who took the keys getting into the car and driving off. (GERHARD SUBTITLE): But I’ll tell you it’s a big emotional shock for a person. Us elderly people, we stay in security complexes that are safe. But when we drive out of here, then anything can happen (MACFARLANE): Gerhard wasn’t the first target… and he won’t be the last for the pickpocket crews. Cars are a valuable prize for these criminals: stripped for parts, used as getaway vehicles or illegally exported. (MACFARLANE): Adriaan is this a syndicate? (ADRIAAN): We know about four groups. We've arrested them, we've chased them. At the beginning it was more like, a “kans-vat” [opportunistic] type of crime. And then they saw it was an easy thing. The amount of cars they are taking goes into a syndicate level immediately. (MACFARLANE): There’s been more than 30 reported cases mostly in Pretoria in just 11 months. And those are the ones we know about. Elsa van der Watt was targeted in April. The footage shows the same shameless set-up. This crew knew what they were shopping for and didn’t waste time. (ELSA SUBTITLE): I can see now how they box you in. (MACFARLANE SUBTITLE): Ok (ELSA SUBTITLE): See they’re looking for something up there, and then they pull it down on purpose. I can see it clearly now. (MACFARLANE SUBTITLE): You’re even helping them! (ELSA SUBTITLE): That’s what I’m saying. From bad to worse. (MACFARLANE SUBTITLE): Is that where the keys were nicked? (ELSA SUBTITLE): Yes, there goes the key. (ELSA SUBTITLE): So easy, right? It’s so unreal. It can’t be. The car can’t just drive off by itself. But hey, this is South Africa. [laughs] (MACFARLANE SUBTITLE): It’s not supposed to be like that. (ELSA SUBTITLE): And in our neighbourhood, four people we know have had their cars taken. The neighbour up the road, three women from our centre - all exactly the same way. (MACFARLANE SUBTITLE): You, they’re sneaky! It’s disgusting what they’re doing. (LIEB): The way they do it, you can see that they are getting away with it for quite substantial time. And and they are well organized. If you look at the number of vehicles left to be recovered, compared to the number of vehicles that's lost, there must be an element of organized crime involved in this, especially in the market receiving these vehicles. (MACFARLANE): To understand the stolen car trade, we approached someone who knows it from the inside. He’s a self-confessed car thief and, while not tied to the pickpocket crews, he knows their market. (CAR THIEF SUBTITLE): You see, a car that comes with keys is like a complete car. (MACFARLANE): It’s the best… (CAR THIEF): It’s the best. (CAR THIEF SUBTITLE): There are no scratches, no broken glass, the ignition hasn’t been damaged. When people see a car like that, they pay good money. (MACFARLANE): The brand doesn’t matter - every car has a buyer. (MACFARLANE SUBTITLE): Where are the different markets? (CAR THIEF SUBTITLE): Yah, any Toyota and legends even Ford Ranger, Raptor – you can name them. Those are the ones that cross the border (MACFARLANE SUBTITLE): And the other ones? What happens with them? (CAR THIEF SUBTITLE): Those are the ones we take to the local scrapyard. And the small cars, those are the ones that keep us from going broke. You get R10 000 to R15 000. But for an SUV that goes to the border, that’s like is R200 000. (MACFARLANE): Older SUVs often get repurposed with fake number plates. That’s what happened to Gerhard’s Honda. It was being used as a getaway vehicle in more pick pocket thefts. In April, a tip-off came in. The car was spotted in an informal settlement outside Pretoria. De Klerk and his team swooped on the thieves. (ADRIAAN): We identified the vehicle on certain identifiable marks on the on the vehicle. As soon as they were driving the car we did a take down on them.. UPSOUND FROM ARREST DASH CAM CLIP. (ADRIAAN): They won't give you information. They won't give up their friends. They are all they take the punishment and tomorrow's another day. (MACFARLANE): Despite being caught with a stolen vehicle, the suspects were released on bail. (MACFARLANE): The biggest issue with cracking this crime trend is it’s near impossible to catch and implicate the whole crew in a single car theft, and even harder to get the charges to stick… (LIEB): The guy that you arrest in the vehicle is in possession of a stolen vehicle.But connecting the other two suspects in the group, connecting them is more difficult. (MACFARLANE): Why isn’t a Sting operation viable in this particular crime trend? (LIEB): It's not like you can predict they will be at the shopping center today. They hop all over the place. So the chances of getting them to basically pickpocket you is, is between all of those shoppers. It's very difficult to do a sting operation in that. (MACFARLANE): And, just like the thieves, these incidents tend to slip through the cracks too, dismissed as petty crime by the police. Often, not even the damning CCTV footage is secured. (GERHARD SUBTITLE): As for the police, they didn’t really seem interested. I even told them we’ve got a video of the incident, if you want to try to identify the people. They said, “No, the investigating officer will contact you if they need it.” And that’s the last I heard - that was that. (LIEB): We are limited in the scope of what we can do. We are mandated by the insurance industry to investigate organized crime impacting the insurance industry. We will then be dependent on our partners in law enforcement to assist us in taking this case to a prosecution level. And, and that is our limitations. We can do a lot of things on our own, but in the end. We need law enforcement. Come on board and then to prosecute this is something else. (MACFARLANE): In the meantime, the money is too big an attraction for the pick pocket squads. (CAR THIEF SUBTITLE): With small cars, you know, if you take it to a scrapyard R20 000 - you’ll get that from a scarpyard. So, once you have a small car, you know you’re going to get R20 000. Even if it's just over R10000, you’ll take it. Because you want to go home with something. (MACFARLANE): And, says the insider, this crime is likely to become more sophisticated. (CAR THIEF SUBTITLE): These are beginners. It’s their first time stealing cars. So, that’s why, they know where to take it for small money. They are still learning the ropes. Especially the ones that are targeting the old people. (MACFARLAN SUBTITLE): They’re still building confidence. (CAR THIEF SUBTITLE): They are still building confidence to reach the next level. (LIEB): If you keep your handbag with in the trolley, with your key sticking out, your cell phone sticking out.If you go into a pub and you sit down with the pub and you put down your wallet and your car key next to you, it is an opportunity to take that key and to take your vehicle. You are going to become a target irrespective of your age (MACFARLANE): Because in this deceptive criminal game, all it takes… is one distraction, one key, and in a heartbeat your car is gone. PROMOS PROMO 1 (MACFARLANE): A slick pick pocket squad is operating in plain sight. (ELSA SUBTITLE): Ek kan nou sien dat hulle jou af kamp. (MACFARLANE): Hitting the same unsuspecting targets - the Elderly. We investigate this shameless scam. PROMO 2 (MACFARLANE): Pick pocketing - once a petty crime, now leveled up… (ADRIAAN): These ones, they take what they get. Whether it's a city golf from 19-voetsek or it's a brand new Mercedes Benz. (MACFARLANE): A streetwise crew is on the loose - and business is good. (LIEB): They target, a certain portion of the population (MACFARLANE): They hunt car keys and target the elderly. We unpack this cunning crime trend. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A slick pick pocket squad is shamelessly targeting the elderly - they ‘re not hunting for wallets, they’re hunting for car keys!
metadata.Unique Selling Point: A NEW CRIME TREND CCTV FOOTAGE ENDEARING OLD CHARACTERS
metadata.Further information: A highly coordinated pickpocket squad is sweeping through shopping centres. They hunt for car keys, not wallets by the time their victims realise what’s happened, the car’s gone. The brand doesn’t matter. But the targets stay the same. The elderly. The MO never changes – it’s super slick - lift the car keys, locate the vehicle, and vanish without a trace. 29 cases in 11 months. CCTV footage showing the MO. A stolen vehicle used as the getaway car in another pickpocket theft - an arrest on camera with the same car, yet the suspects were released. As the victims pile up. The evidence stacks up but still, the pickpocket squad is out there, ready to pounce again.
